In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vasculature in the V-SVVZ is not intrinsically different than in the cortex, and that diffusible cortical vascular signals can support the V-SVZZ stem cell lineage.
the vascular niche in the adult brain is not a homogenous entity and its contribution to stem cell behavior is region-specific.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vascular system is an important component in the adult stem cell niche and that vascular cells from different regions of the brain can differentially influence stem cell behavior.
the vasculature is a major source of mitogenic and neurogenic factors in the brain and that the effect of these factors is not uniform in different brain regions.
the adult neural stem/progenitor cells (NS/PCs) reside in a specialized microenvironment (niche) in the adult brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endothelial and pericytes derived from the V-SVz and cortex differentially regulate the adult neural stem cells.
endothelial cells and, surprisingly, pericytes from non-neurogenic areas of the brain are as effective as vascular cells from the V-SVVZ at promoting the proliferation of V-SVZ neural stem cells.
the adult brain is a mosaic of different vascular microenvironments that can differentially support stem cell behavior.
